paragraphs.text: Solomon’s altar was four times as large as this: to teach that as our peace and prosperity is more than others, so should our service in a due proportion.
To bind the beasts unto, that were to be slain in sacrifice. {Psa 118:27} And to signify the power of Christ’s priesthood. {Hab 3:4}
The brass kept the wood; so did the deity of Christ keep his humanity from being consumed by the fire of God’s wrath, wherein it was roasted.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt overlay it with brass.

paragraphs.text: These several instruments figured the ministry of the word, say some; the sundry callings that Christ hath in his Church, say others, for her edification.
Which served for a hearth, and represented Christ bearing the fire of his Father’s displeasure.
As ever ready to remove. Here we have no assured settlement.
This outer court signified the visible Church, where hypocrites also come to the external worships. Doeg may set his foot as far as David.
In allusion whereunto, the Church is called the "pillar and stay of truth." {1Ti 3:15}
The nearer things were unto God the more precious they were: and e contra.
paragraphs.anchor: Their hooks shall be of silver, and their sockets of brass.

paragraphs.text: Signifying the precious gifts and graces of the Spirit in godly ministers, whose lips must both preserve knowledge, and present it to the people.

Signifying, saith one, how with much labour and affliction the light of God’s word is to be prepared, and with patience preached and made to shine in his Church. {2Co 1:4; 2Co 2:4; 2Co 11:21; 2Co 11:23-25 1Th 2:9}
